hazards.label: Heat
hazards.effect_note: The twin's heat leads (ageing, derating, chiller capacity) work through performance, not physical damage; pointer to the outage-as-performance work, no curve (discussion 04 §6).

hazards.label: Icing
hazards.effect_note: Two leads in the twin: snow load on the venting panels (physical, L) and cold limiting the charge rate until heated (performance, L). No hazard cell; the C-172 snow-and-ice reasoning applies (discussion 04 §6).

hazards.label: Lightning
hazards.effect_note: No hazard cell exists; the twin carries Medium surge leads on the electronics (discussion 04 §6).

split.sentence: These cells split the substation differently: the cells name different numbers of parts: flood 1, convective wind 1, hurricane wind 1 and wildfire 2; flood treats whole station (fenced assembly) as one unit that spans 345 kv yard: breakers, disconnects, bus, instrument transformers, deadends, 138 kv yard: breakers, disconnects, bus, instrument transformers, deadends, autotransformers, oil containment and firewall, relays, control house, station battery, scada, station service, control cable and site work, access road, drainage and lightning shielding; wildfire binds 8 equipment rows ($13.0M, 48 % of the fenced station) and withholds the rest; the other hazards use one curve for the whole station. Hazard's substation reference budget ($27.35M fenced station) sets the rows; three hazards use one curve for the whole station, wildfire binds the equipment rows only.
